private_notes.observations: No prior rate cards or hour allocations are available, so demand and competitor pricing are unknown. Fully loaded cost is $200 per hour.
private_notes.plan: Start with a competitive rate that provides a meaningful margin. Use subsequent published rate cards and allocated hours to estimate price sensitivity and adjust for long-run profit.

private_notes.observations: At $300, we received 852 hours and earned approximately $85,164. Both other panel firms charged $325. We have only one quarter of data, so the effect of a rate change on hours is unknown.
private_notes.plan: Raise the rate modestly to $310 while remaining below both competitors. Compare next quarter's hours and profit with Q1 before making a larger adjustment.

private_notes.observations: At $325 in Q1, we received approximately 517 hours and earned $64,569. One competitor charged $300 and the other $325; one quarter does not establish how sensitive allocations are to price.
private_notes.plan: Increase the rate modestly to test whether a higher margin offsets any reduction in hours. Compare Q2 hours and the next rate card before adjusting further.

private_notes.observations: In Q1, a $325 rate yielded 517 allocated hours and approximately $64,569 in profit. Competing rates were $300 and $325. One quarter does not establish how sensitive allocations are to price.
private_notes.plan: Test a modest rate increase to learn whether the higher margin offsets any loss of hours. Compare Q2 hours and profit with Q1 before making further adjustments.

private_notes.observations: At $310 in Q2, Arden & Cole received 884 hours and earned $97,219, up from 852 hours and $85,164 at $300 in Q1. Both competitors raised their rates from $325 to $340, so we remained the lowest-priced firm.
private_notes.plan: Raise our rate while retaining a discount to the latest published competitor rates. Monitor whether the higher margin offsets any change in allocated hours, recognizing that competitor rates may change.

private_notes.observations: Raising our rate from $325 in Q1 to $340 in Q2 coincided with hours declining from 517 to 485, while quarterly profit rose from about $64,569 to $67,907. Competitor rates also increased, so the effect of our rate alone is uncertain.
private_notes.plan: Test another modest increase and monitor allocated hours and profit. Adjust based on observed demand rather than assuming the Q1–Q2 change was entirely caused by our pricing.

private_notes.observations: Raising our rate from $325 to $340 increased quarterly profit from about $64,569 to $67,907, despite hours falling from 517 to 485. Competitor rates also rose, so the effect of our price change alone is uncertain.
private_notes.plan: Raise the rate modestly again to test whether additional margin outweighs any further decline in allocated hours. Monitor both profit and hours before considering a larger move.

private_notes.observations: Competitors raised rates by $15 in each of the last two quarters, while our $25–$30 discount coincided with roughly 850–885 allocated hours. Our quarterly profit rose as our rate increased.
private_notes.plan: Raise our rate by $15 to $340, preserving approximately a $30 discount if competitors continue their recent pattern. Reassess allocation and profit next quarter.

private_notes.observations: Profit rose from $64,569 in Q1 to $73,309 in Q3 despite a modest decline in allocated hours. Other panel firms also raised their rates, so the effect of our own increases on demand is uncertain.
private_notes.plan: Increase the rate modestly again, then assess whether the resulting profit gain outweighs any further loss of hours. Avoid assuming competitors will continue raising rates.

private_notes.observations: Profit rose each quarter as our rate increased from $325 to $355, despite allocated hours declining from 517 to 473. Arden & Cole has remained $30 below our rate; Birchwood Hale has matched it.
private_notes.plan: Raise the rate by another $15 to test whether the higher margin continues to outweigh lost hours. Reassess after seeing Q4 allocation and the panel rate card.

private_notes.observations: Profit increased each quarter as our rate rose from $300 to $340. Our last two $15 increases coincided with modest declines in allocated hours, while the other firms each raised rates by $15 per quarter.
private_notes.plan: Test a larger increase while remaining below the other firms’ latest published rates. Compare the resulting hours and profit with Q4 before making another adjustment.

private_notes.observations: Profit increased in each of Q1–Q4 despite modest declines in allocated hours as our rate rose from $325 to $370. The other firms also raised their rates, but their future pricing is uncertain.
private_notes.plan: Raise our rate modestly to test whether higher margin continues to outweigh lost hours. Reassess using next quarter’s allocation and profit rather than assuming the other firms will increase their rates.

private_notes.observations: Profit rose each quarter as our rate increased by $15, despite a modest decline in allocated hours. At $370 in Q4, we received 458 hours and earned $77,787. The other firms' published rates also increased, but Meridian's allocation formula remains unknown.
private_notes.plan: Raise our rate by $15 to $385. Compare the resulting profit and hours with Q4 before deciding whether to raise it further.

private_notes.observations: Q5’s increase to $365 reduced allocated hours to 705; profit was $116,311, slightly below Q4’s $116,724. Both other firms have raised rates by $15 each quarter and charged $385 in Q5.
private_notes.plan: Raise the rate modestly to $370 to seek a better balance between margin and allocated hours. Compare Q6 hours and profit with Q4 and Q5 before adjusting again.

private_notes.observations: Profit rose each quarter, reaching $87,416 in Q5 at a $385 rate. Hours increased from 458 to 473 in Q5 despite our $15 rate increase, though competitors’ rates also rose, so the effect of our rate alone is unclear.
private_notes.plan: Increase our rate modestly to $400 and assess the resulting hours and profit next quarter. Base future adjustments on our own profitability rather than assuming competitors will continue raising rates.

private_notes.observations: Profit rose in every quarter through Q5. At $385, allocated hours increased to 473 from 458 in Q4, despite our $15 rate increase; the other firms also raised rates.
private_notes.plan: Raise the rate another $15 to $400. Continue testing incremental increases while monitoring allocated hours and profit; reassess if higher rates materially reduce our work.

private_notes.observations: Q6 profit rose to $128,475 at a $370 rate, above Q4 and Q5. Maintaining roughly a $30 discount to the other firms has generally supported strong hour allocations; their rates have increased by $15 each quarter.
private_notes.plan: Set $385, preserving the approximate $30 discount if competitors continue their trend. Review Q7 hours and profit before considering another increase.

private_notes.observations: Profit peaked at $87,416 in Q5 at a $385 rate, then fell to $82,951 in Q6 at $400 as allocated hours dropped from 473 to 415. Competitor rates and allocations have changed, so the precise effect of our rate is uncertain.
private_notes.plan: Set $390 to test whether a modest reduction recovers enough hours to improve profit. Reassess using our realized hours and profit next quarter.

private_notes.observations: Profit rose through Q5 at $385, then fell in Q6 at $400 as allocated hours dropped from 473 to 415. The other firms' published rates have generally risen alongside ours, so the Q6 decline does not establish that $400 alone caused the drop.
private_notes.plan: Test a smaller $10 increase to $410. Compare next quarter's hours and profit with Q6 before deciding whether to keep raising the rate or pull back.

private_notes.observations: Q7's $385 rate left us only $5 below the lowest competitor; allocated hours fell to 615 and profit to $113,770, versus 756 hours and $128,475 profit in Q6 at $370.
private_notes.plan: Reduce the rate to restore a meaningful discount to the lowest panel rate and seek higher total profit through increased hours. Reassess after seeing Q8 allocation and the new rate card.

private_notes.observations: At $390 in Q7, we received 556 hours and earned $105,725, our strongest quarter. The improvement over Q6 coincided with both our rate reduction and competitors' rate increases, so their individual effects are unclear.
private_notes.plan: Set $395 to test a modest margin increase while remaining close to the rate that produced strong Q7 volume. Compare next quarter's hours and panel rates before making a larger change.

private_notes.observations: Profit peaked at $87,416 in Q5 with a $385 rate. Raising it to $400 and then $410 reduced both allocated hours and profit; in Q7, Birchwood Hale also lowered its rate to $390.
private_notes.plan: Return to $385 to improve competitiveness and test whether regained hours outweigh the lower margin. Reassess after observing the next allocation and rate card.

private_notes.observations: Q8’s $375 rate earned $113,064 with only a $10 discount to the lowest competing rate. Q6 earned $128,475 at $370 with a $30 discount. Allocations vary, but a larger discount appears worth testing.
private_notes.plan: Set $365 to restore a meaningful discount while preserving a $165 hourly margin. Reassess profit and hours against the next panel rate card.

private_notes.observations: At $395 in Q8, profit fell to $84,451 as Calder Rowe cut its rate to $385. Q7’s unusually high hours at $390 coincided with higher competing rates, so its volume may not repeat.
private_notes.plan: Set $385 to improve competitiveness against Calder Rowe while preserving a $185 hourly margin. Reassess volume and competitor rates next quarter.

private_notes.observations: Q8's $385 rate produced 529 hours and $97,859 profit, the highest quarterly profit so far. At $400–$410 in Q6–Q7, hours and profit were lower. Q8's other panel rates were $375 and $395.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $385 to preserve the strong Q8 combination of margin and allocated hours. Reassess after the next allocation and rate card.

private_notes.observations: At $365 with both competitors at $385, Arden & Cole received 705 hours and earned $116,311 in both Q5 and Q9. The higher $370 rate performed best when competitors charged $400, but their latest rates are $385.

private_notes.observations: At $385, the firm earned $87,416 in both Q5 and Q9, with 473 hours allocated each time. The higher $395 rate earned $84,451 in Q8. Q7's unusually strong result at $390 coincided with higher competitor rates.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $385 to preserve a $185 hourly margin and the allocation observed under the most recent rate card. Reassess if competitor pricing or allocated hours change materially.

private_notes.plan: Hold at $385 while the rate card and allocation remain stable. Reassess if competitor rates or allocated hours change materially.

private_notes.observations: At $385, profit was $87,416 in each of Q5, Q9, and Q10 with comparable panel rates. A $400 rate yielded $82,951 in Q6, while $410 yielded $78,330 in Q7. Q8 produced $97,859 at $385 when competing rates were higher.
private_notes.plan: Hold $385. This rate has delivered strong, repeatable profit; reassess if the panel rate card or allocated hours change materially.

private_notes.observations: At $385, the last three quarters each produced 473 allocated hours and approximately $87,416 profit. The competitors’ rates have also remained unchanged at $365 and $385.

private_notes.observations: At $385, the last three quarters each produced 473 hours and approximately $87,416 profit. The other firms' rates have also been unchanged.

private_notes.observations: At $365 against two $385 competitors, Arden & Cole has consistently received 705 hours and earned $116,311 per quarter from Q9 through Q12.

private_notes.observations: At $385, allocated hours and the panel rate card have remained unchanged for four consecutive quarters; quarterly profit has been $87,416. The $410 rate in Q7 produced lower profit.

private_notes.observations: At $385, the panel rate card and allocation have remained stable for five quarters: 473 hours and about $87,416 profit per quarter. Past increases above $385 reduced hours and profit.

private_notes.observations: Arden & Cole cut its rate from $365 to $274 in Q14, while ours stayed at $385. Our allocated hours fell from 473 to 167, reducing quarterly profit from $87,416 to $30,967. Birchwood Hale remained at $385.
private_notes.plan: Lower our rate substantially to regain hours while preserving a meaningful margin above the $200 hourly cost. Assess the resulting allocation and next quarter’s rate card before adjusting again.

private_notes.observations: At $320 in Q15, with competitors at $320 and $325, profit fell to $77,252. The $274 rate in Q14 drew substantially more hours but produced only $114,050 in profit and preceded competitors’ rate cuts. Earlier, $365 with competitors at $385 generated $116,311 per quarter.
private_notes.plan: Set a modest discount to the latest competitor rates without repeating the steep Q14 cut. Assess both profit and competitor responses next quarter before changing course.

private_notes.observations: At $320 in Q15, we received 644 hours and earned $77,252, with competitors at $320 and $325. The previous $385 rate performed poorly when Arden cut to $274; Arden has since returned to $320.

private_notes.observations: At $325 in Q15, we received 583 hours and earned $72,813 while both competitors charged $320. The earlier $385 rate earned more when competing rates were higher, but performed poorly when Arden cut to $274.

private_notes.observations: Q16's $310 rate against two $325 competitors earned $83,115. The earlier $274 cut generated substantial hours but was followed by competitors cutting their rates sharply. Recent results suggest a modest discount is preferable to another deep cut.

private_notes.observations: At $325 in Q16, we earned about $70,000 with competitors at $310 and $325. At $320 in Q15, we earned about $77,000 when competitor rates were $320 and $325. The Q14 allocation fell sharply when one competitor charged $274 while we charged $385.
private_notes.plan: Set $310 to match the lowest recently observed panel rate and seek more hours while retaining a $110 hourly margin. Reassess profitability after the next allocation and rate card.

private_notes.observations: At $325, Calder Rowe earned about $70,000 in Q16 despite Arden & Cole lowering its rate to $310. The sharp workload loss at $385 in Q14 shows the risk of a large price gap.

private_notes.observations: Q17's $305 rate earned $77,072, below Q16's $83,115 at $310. Competitor rates have fallen substantially since Q13, so the earlier $365 results are not directly comparable.
private_notes.plan: Set $310 to recover some margin without a large increase relative to the current panel. Monitor the next rate card and allocated hours before making further adjustments.

private_notes.observations: At $310 in Q17, we received 664 hours and earned $73,058. The other firms charged $305 and $325. A $385 rate produced only 167 hours when a competitor dropped to $274 in Q14, indicating substantial sensitivity to relative rates.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $310 to stay close to the lowest observed competitor while preserving a $110 hourly margin. Reassess after seeing the next allocation and rate card.

private_notes.observations: At $325, profit fell from about $73,000 in Q15 to $61,503 in Q17 as competing rates declined to $305 and $310. The current $15–$20 rate disadvantage appears to be costing hours.
private_notes.plan: Set $305 to improve competitiveness while preserving a $105 hourly margin. Reassess whether the additional hours offset the lower margin after Q18.

private_notes.observations: The panel’s rates have fallen from $385–$410 to $305–$310. My $310 rate in Q18 earned $67,269 on 612 hours, down from $77,072 at $305 in Q17.
private_notes.plan: Set $305, matching the lowest rate on the latest card without a sharp cut that could prompt another round of reductions. Reassess hours and competitor rates next quarter.

private_notes.observations: At $310 in Q18, we received 612 hours and earned $67,269. Calder Rowe reduced its rate to $305, making our rate the highest on the panel. Recent allocations suggest that even a small rate disadvantage can materially reduce our hours.
private_notes.plan: Set $305 to match the lowest recently observed panel rate while retaining a $105 hourly margin. Reassess profitability and allocation next quarter.

private_notes.observations: At $305 in Q18, Calder Rowe earned $70,964 on 676 hours, up from $61,503 at $325 in Q17. Both competitors charged $310 in Q18, so the lower rate appears to have gained enough hours to offset its smaller margin.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $305 to preserve the demonstrated volume advantage while earning $105 per hour. Reassess if competitors change their rates or allocated hours fall.

private_notes.observations: At $305 with both competitors also at $305 in Q19, we earned $66,676. A steep cut to $274 in Q14 briefly increased hours but was followed by substantial panel-wide rate reductions and lower profits.
private_notes.plan: Hold at $305 rather than provoke another round of cuts. Monitor whether competitors stabilize or raise rates before testing an increase.

private_notes.observations: At $305, with both other firms also charging $305, we received 635 hours and earned approximately $66,676. Recent modest rate reductions increased our allocated hours, though profit has declined from earlier quarters.
private_notes.plan: Test a small unilateral reduction to $300 to seek additional hours while retaining a $100 hourly margin. Reassess realized profit and competitors’ published rates next quarter.

private_notes.observations: At $305 with both competitors also at $305, we received 635 hours and earned $66,676 in Q19. Charging $325 when competitors were near $305–$310 yielded lower profit in Q17. The recent rate card has stabilized at $305.
